stations.title: Anaphylaxis Management
stations.task: Manage a patient with acute anaphylaxis after food exposure

patient.name: Lisa Chang
patient.opening: (Wheezing, flushed, clutching throat) I can't breathe... my lips are swelling...

mustAsk: Have you had this reaction before?
bonus: Ask about timing from exposure to symptoms

questions.question: What is the first-line treatment?
questions.answer: IM epinephrine 0.3-0.5 mg (1:1000) in the anterolateral thigh, repeat every 5-15 minutes

stations.title: Sepsis Recognition and Initial Management
stations.task: Recognize and initiate management for a patient presenting with sepsis

patient.name: Robert Kim
patient.opening: (Confused, febrile) I don't feel well... my wife brought me in...

hiddenProfile.diagnosis: Sepsis secondary to urinary tract infection
hiddenProfile.vitalSigns: BP 88/55, HR 118, RR 28, O2 sat 95%, Temp 39.2°C, GCS 13

bonus: Ask about recent procedures or catheterization

questions.question: What is the immediate management in the first hour?
questions.answer: Blood cultures, lactate, broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., piperacillin-tazobactam), 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus, vasopressors if hypotensive after fluids
